q: A corporate client wants the carbon footprint of their conference at our hotel. How do we calculate it?
title: Conference footprint at a hotel
short: Add three parts: meeting space used (square metres x hours x your footprint per square metre-hour), guest room nights x your footprint per occupied room night, and meals x a per-meal food factor. Divide by delegates for a per guest figure. Guests' travel to the venue is the client's to add.
audience: Hotels and banquet venues hosting corporate conferences and weddings

sections.h: Build your two hotel factors once a year
ol: Total the hotel's Scope 1 and 2 for the year: electricity, DG diesel, kitchen LPG or PNG, boiler fuel and refrigerant top-ups.
Split it between guest rooms and meeting space by floor area. The Hotel Carbon Measurement Initiative (HCMI) uses this approach.
Rooms factor: the rooms share divided by occupied room nights.
Meeting factor: the meeting share divided by meeting area times the hours the space is available in the year.

ul: Meeting space: each hall's area x hours booked, including set-up.
Rooms: room nights booked for the event, not the number of guests.
Food: meals served x a per-meal factor for ingredients. Kitchen fuel is already in your hotel total, so use an ingredients-only factor to avoid counting it twice.

sections.h: What the client does with your figure
p: For the client it is Scope 3: room nights in Category 6, business travel, and the event package in Category 1, purchased services. For you it is part of your own Scope 1 and 2, already counted. Delegates' flights and cars are the client's to calculate.

ISO 20121:2024 is a management system standard for event sustainability. It asks the organiser to manage impacts, but it does not set a carbon formula. Give them your figure, the method and the year of your hotel data.

example.title: Worked example: a two day conference, 200 delegates (illustrative inputs)
lines: Floor split: meeting 15% = 349,440 kg; rooms 85% = 1,980,160 kg
Meeting factor: 349,440 / (2,000 m2 x 4,380 hours) = 0.0399 kg per m2-hour
Rooms factor: 1,980,160 / 60,000 occupied room nights = 33.0 kg per room night
Event: ballroom 600 m2 x 18 h x 0.0399 = 431 kg; 150 room nights x 33.0 = 4,950 kg; 600 meals x 1.5 kg CO2e (assumed, ingredients) = 900 kg
Total: 431 + 4,950 + 900 = 6,281 kg, about 31.4 kg per delegate
example.note: Energy lines are CO2; food is CO2e. The meal factor and floor split are assumptions for illustration.

senseible: Senseible reads the hotel's electricity bills (billing period, tariff, sanctioned load and units, at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CEA version 21.0) and fuel invoices such as diesel and LPG (IPCC 2006 defaults) into Scope 1 and 2, the annual total these event factors start from. Floor areas, room nights and meals come from your records.
